description: Use for Continual-ARC puzzles. Infer rules from demos.
---

# Continual-ARC reasoning

Use this skill for ARC-style tasks in a recurring puzzle stream, especially when the interaction allows requesting demonstrations and submission attempts are costly.

## Workflow

1. **Parse the interaction contract.** Preserve the required response format exactly; choose one action per turn. Treat demo requests and wrong submissions as costly, and do not spend either without a reason.
2. **Inspect demonstrations comparatively.** Track dimensions, background, marker/object colors, and every changed cell. Form a compact rule that explains all examples, rather than fitting only the most visually salient region.
3. **Separate evidence from hypothesis.** Prefer a rule that predicts multiple independent changes in each demo. If ambiguity remains and the cost is justified, request another demo before submitting.
4. **Apply the rule mechanically.** Use a small script or structured representation for large grids when useful. Preserve original marker cells and untouched background; do not rely on manual transcription for a long output.
5. **Validate before submitting.** Check row count, column count, allowed values, unchanged source cells where appropriate, and consistency of every changed cell with the inferred transformation. Re-read the exact test input when constructing the result.
6. **Submit only the requested artifact.** In strict ARC interaction formats, avoid explanatory text if the protocol calls for a single action object.

## Common geometric transformation: connect aligned markers

A recurring pattern is a sparse set of same-color marker cells on a uniform background. Demonstrations may show a third color filling the straight gaps between consecutive markers that share a row or column. See [references/aligned-marker-lines.md](references/aligned-marker-lines.md) for how to infer and implement this rule, including boundary and overlap checks.

### Validated recurrence: task-83eba677 horizontal gap fill

For task-83eba677, fill only the cells strictly between consecutive same-color markers in each row with color 2. Do not fill vertical alignments, even when markers share a column. Preserve marker cells and all unrelated background cells. A further accepted 13×17 test had background 8, marker 0, with multiple horizontal chains; precisely the cells between consecutive 0s in each row became 2, while vertical alignments and isolated markers were left unchanged. This holds for single-cell gaps as well as longer gaps: a newly accepted 18×24 test (background 4, markers 8) had horizontal marker runs spanning gaps of several cells; every intervening cell between consecutive 8s in a row became 2, with other cells unchanged. Prior fresh cases also confirmed background 6/marker 1 and background 3/marker 5, plus an accepted 17×13 background 1/marker 8 case (29 changed cells). The 5×6 case had pairs at row 2 columns 0/2 and row 4 columns 1/3 (0-based), yielding 2 at the intervening cells only. A fresh accepted 20×29 test used background 3 and markers 4; fill 2 strictly between consecutive 4s in each row, ignoring vertical alignments. The output changed exactly 50 gap cells and preserved all markers and other background. Infer fill color 2, not from background or marker color.

## Full-line recoloring (validated task-5ebf4030)

For task-5ebf4030, identify complete horizontal rows and vertical columns consisting entirely of the same non-background color (color 7 in the demo; color 3 and 6 in fresh tests). Recolor every cell of each such full line to 2. Preserve all other cells, including occurrences of the line color outside complete lines. A newly solved 6×27 test had background 1 and line color 6; the only full row was row 2 (0-based), and full columns were 11, 19, and 25. Recolor those four lines to 2 while retaining partial 6s elsewhere. The demo had a full vertical line and a full horizontal line; the fresh 28x9 test had two full vertical lines and two full horizontal lines. This criterion reproduced the demo output and was accepted on fresh tests with two full vertical and two full horizontal lines (28x9), and on a 20x10 test with complete horizontal rows 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 and complete vertical column 4 (0-based). The latter confirms that full lines are recognized by the uniform line color even when the surrounding grid is a mixed 8/6 field; all complete 6-lines become 2. A second fresh 21x25 test used color 5, with complete rows 4 and 13 (0-based) and complete columns 10, 12, 17, and 22; all these lines became 2 while all other cells were preserved. Another accepted 19×24 recurrence had background 5 and line color 7, with full rows 7, 14, and 16 and full columns 12 and 17 (zero-based); precisely these lines were recolored to 2, including their intersections, while all partial 7s were preserved. Another accepted 9×7 test used background 6 and line color 0: full rows 4 and 8 and full column 5 (zero-based) were recolored to 2; all other 0s, including partial occurrences, were preserved. This confirms the uniform-line rule applies when the line color is zero. A further accepted 5×22 case had background 4 and line color 3; full row 4 and full columns 6 and 15 alone were recolored to 2, with all partial 3s preserved. A further accepted 28×12 recurrence had background 3 and line color 4, with full rows 2 and 9 and full columns 0 and 8; precisely those four complete lines were recolored to 2, preserving all partial 4s elsewhere. Apply only to full single-color lines, not merely dense or partial alignments.

## Validated motif-stamping substrate

For task-868ab99b, extract the foreground mask of the uniquely colored seed motif and stamp that mask in its seed color at every translation where **all occupied mask offsets overlay 0-cells**. The dominant field color can vary (e.g. 8 or 9) and is not the placement substrate; requiring mask offsets to match the dominant color is wrong. Ignore mask bounding-box cells that are not foreground, and preserve all cells outside the stamped mask. This rule reproduced the provided demos and a fresh test.

For task-7a5e2600, do not assume a fixed mask across instances. Extract the foreground mask from that instance's seed and stamp it in the seed color at every translation where all occupied offsets overlay cells of color 0; replace only those zero cells and preserve every other cell. Validated examples show the mask varies: demo 1 had a 7-cell 4×3 mask with offsets {(0,1),(1,0),(1,2),(2,0),(2,1),(3,1),(3,2)}; demo 2 and the accepted fresh test had a 9-cell 4×4 mask with offsets {(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1)}. In both variants, requiring only occupied mask offsets to overlay zeros reproduced the demonstrated / accepted transformations; do not require the whole bounding box to be zero.

Do not infer motif substrate rules universally; for other tasks, determine the mask, seed color, and placement substrate from demonstrations.

### Validated recurrence: task-7a5e2600 motif stamping

Do not assume a fixed mask across instances: extract the seed foreground mask anew from each instance. Stamp that mask in the seed color at every translation where all occupied offsets overlay cells of color 0; replace only those zero cells and preserve all other cells, including the seed and nonzero field. Two validated mask variants: demo 1 used a 7-cell 4×3 mask with offsets `{(0,1),(1,0),(1,2),(2,0),(2,1),(3,1),(3,2)}`; demo 2 and the accepted fresh test used a 9-cell 4×4 mask with offsets `{(0,0),(0,1),(0,2),(1,1),(1,2),(1,3),(2,1),(3,0),(3,1)}`. For each, requiring only the occupied offsets to overlay zeros reproduced the demonstrated / accepted transformation. Do not require the whole bounding box to be zero.

## Periodic stripe completion (validated task-eca8fe17)

For task-eca8fe17, demos show a sparse periodic color field encoded by colored full stripes/lines. Infer the repeating cycle and orientation from the line markers, then tile that cycle across the whole grid, replacing zeros as well as preserving the encoded colors. Examples: horizontal stripes can encode a row-period cycle (period 6 in the 8x8 demo; period 7 in the 11x11 demo), while parallel slope-−1 diagonal stripes encode phases of a cycle by `row+column mod period` (period 4 in the 28x28 demo). For fresh tests, do not assume one orientation or period; identify line direction and phase-color mapping from the current input/demos. Validated mappings include: a 28×28 parallel slope−1 diagonal field with period 4 encoded by `(r+c) mod 4`, phases 0→4, 1→2, 2→1; and task-eca8fe17 fresh tests where `(r+c) mod 3` mapped phases 0→4, 1→2, 2→1. A separate 8×8 test had parallel slope+1 diagonal markers, period 5 encoded by `(r−c) mod 5`, with phases 0→1, 1→9, 2→6, 3→5, 4→3; fill every cell using this cycle while preserving the encoded marker colors. A successful 23×23 test had a period-3 slope+1 diagonal field, with `c−r mod 3 = 0,1,2` mapped to colors `6,6,2` respectively (equivalently, color 2 at `c−r ≡ 2 mod 3`, color 6 elsewhere); marker 2s fixed that phase and overlapping 6 diagonal bands confirmed the remaining phase assignments. Fill every cell with the periodic field, not merely extending gaps.

### Confirmed task-eca8fe17 horizontal full-row cycle fresh test
A 7×7 test had each row uniform, with row colors `[0,9,3,6,9,8,0]`. Correct output row colors were `[8,9,3,6,9,8,9]`, i.e. repeat the six-row cycle `[8,9,3,6,9,8]` from row 0. The colored rows at indices 1–5 validated this period and phase; zeros at rows 0 and 6 were unknown slots, not cycle colors. Accepted. Infer the smallest supported periodic sequence and fill zero rows; preserve the demonstrated cycle colors.

## Noisy rectangular-field reconstruction (validated task-7a9d058a)

The grid is a patchwork of uniform rectangular color regions on a uniform background, corrupted by sparse arbitrary noise symbols. Recover each rectangle's exact bounds from repeated full spans and intact runs, then recolor every cell inside it (including noise/outliers) to that region's color. Set every non-rectangle cell to the background, including isolated colored speckles. Do not treat one digit as globally noisy, and do not assume 0 means empty: 0 can be the legitimate color of an entire region. Demos validate this: one has background 9, a 0 rectangle at rows 1–7/cols 4–9, a 3 rectangle at rows 12–15/cols 8–10, and a 0 rectangle at rows 14–20/cols 3–4, with many arbitrary intrusions and exterior speckles; another has background 3, a 6 rectangle at rows 2–5/cols 3–5 and 8 rectangles at rows 0–3/cols 8–9 and rows 6–7/cols 7–10, with stray values removed/restored. Fresh accepted 20×29 test (background 6) has rectangles: color 2 at (r0–3,c0–1), (r2–8,c6–8), (r5–11,c1–2), (r6–8,c10–14), (r6–7,c27–28), (r13–19,c13–19), (r15–19,c3–4); color 4 at (r0–4,c12–14), (r0–3,c16–21), (r0–2,c23–26), (r15–17,c7–11), (r17–18,c21–24); color 5 at (r5–11,c16–22), (r9–13,c24–28), (r9–11,c5–7), and (r16–17,c26–28). Coordinates are zero-based, endpoints inclusive. This accepted test corrected the rejected candidate by extending the upper 4 field to row 3 and the far-right 5 field through row 13; it also established a separate 5 rectangle at rows 9–11, cols 5–7. Carefully audit every outer boundary; an adjacent singleton must not extend a region unless the rectangle's repeated runs establish it. Validate every inferred rectangle against all demos, ensure rectangles do not overlap, check all reliable object-color cells are accounted for, and clear every exterior anomaly to the background before submission.

### Additional accepted fresh test (task-7a9d058a, 14×21)
Background 4. Rectangles, with zero-based inclusive bounds: color 1 at rows 0–1/cols 3–6; color 0 at rows 3–4/cols 0–3; color 5 at rows 1–3/cols 14–16; color 0 at rows 6–12/cols 13–14, rows 7–12/cols 9–10, rows 9–11/cols 3–7, and rows 9–13/cols 16–19. Restore every cell inside each rectangle to its field color; all cells outside these regions become 4, including arbitrary singletons (e.g. the 7 at row 0/col 20, the 2 at row 2/col 20, and the 9 at row 13/col 15). This test followed one incorrect candidate: its row 9–12/cols 3–7 rectangle was too tall, its row 9–12/cols 9–10 rectangle was too short at the top, and it missed the extensions of the row 6–12/cols 13–14 region and row 9–13/cols 16–19 region. The accepted correction demonstrates why each rectangle's top and bottom edges must be checked against sparse contaminated runs; do not infer bounds merely from the densest rows. Note: the older 20×29 case listed above has conflicting status in the supporting audit (which says correctness feedback was unavailable); treat that example as unverified unless independently reconfirmed.

### Additional accepted fresh test (task-7a9d058a, 29×21)
Background 2. Reconstruct and fill these zero-based inclusive rectangles, correcting all interior noise and clearing exterior speckles: color 0 at rows 7–9/cols 4–6, rows 23–28/cols 4–9, and rows 23–26/cols 12–13; color 9 at rows 6–9/cols 12–18 and rows 18–22/cols 0–2; color 5 at rows 16–20/cols 5–8. All other cells are background 2, including sparse non-2 values outside the rectangles. The accepted submission validates the contaminated rectangular-field reconstruction rule on a large grid with multiple rectangles of the same color, multiple legitimate region colors (including 0), and many isolated exterior speckles.

## Comparing aligned panels with sparse zero-cells

When a divider separates aligned panels, infer the cellwise predicate from the demos rather than assuming that each panel's modal color defines its semantic background. In the validated task-192705d2 pattern, output a 2 where both corresponding input cells are nonzero, and 0 otherwise. The panels can have different dominant colors (for example, 5 on one side and 0 on the other; or 8 and 6 on a fresh test), while literal 0 is the empty-cell value. Thus implement `left_cell != 0 and right_cell != 0`; do not implement “both are non-background relative to each panel’s mode,” which incorrectly selects shared zeros in a 8/6 test. This was confirmed by a rejected shared-zero candidate followed by a correct nonzero-overlap submission. A fresh 4×9 recurrence had a single divider column (color 1) between two 4×4 panels; exclude the divider and produce a 4×4 mask by the same nonzero-overlap predicate. A further accepted 7×27 test used a full horizontal divider row (color 6) between 3×27 panels (dominant colors 1 and 9); exclude the divider and output the 3×27 nonzero-overlap mask. This confirms the same predicate applies to horizontal as well as vertical panel splits. Another accepted 10×15 recurrence had a full vertical color-8 divider at column 7, with 10×7 panels; left cells were sparse 6s and right cells sparse 4s. The accepted 10×7 output placed 2 exactly at nonzero overlaps: zero-based (r4,c5), (r5,c6), and (r7,c6), with all other cells 0. This reinforces that different nonzero colors count, and do not align the right panel including the divider. Always replay the predicate against the demo outputs and exact fresh input before submitting.

## Validated task-65d930f4 three-band mirror tiling

For task-65d930f4, expand an H×W input to 3H×2W. Each output row is the input row mirrored left-to-right, concatenated with the original row. Stack three vertical bands: input rows bottom-to-top, then top-to-bottom, then bottom-to-top. Equivalently, output row source indices are `H-1..0`, `0..H-1`, `H-1..0`. Preserve all source cell values; this is a geometric reflection/tiling rule, not recoloring. Confirmed on the 5×4 demo (15×8 output), 9×11 demo (27×22 output), fresh 3×9 (9×18), 1×12 (3×24), 9×3 (27×6), and accepted fresh 4×8 (12×16) tests. The 9×11 demo directly confirms the three bands: rows 0–8 use input rows 8→0; rows 9–17 use input rows 0→8; rows 18–26 use input rows 8→0. Every row is source reversed followed by source unchanged. A further accepted fresh 7×6 test had rows `[9,1,4,1,3,5]`, `[5,7,1,5,7,5]`, `[1,4,4,5,5,9]`, `[1,5,4,5,7,4]`, `[5,5,6,5,5,5]`, `[5,1,5,5,7,5]`, `[5,5,6,5,6,5]`; it produced a 21×12 output under the same rule: row source order `[6,5,4,3,2,1,0,0,1,2,3,4,5,6,6,5,4,3,2,1,0]`, each source row reversed then original. This confirms the rule with a mixed-color 7×6 input. The accepted 9×3 test confirms short narrow inputs still use the same 3H×2W transformation. For the 1×12 input `[5,0,1,3,4,3,7,6,9,3,2,8]`, each of the three output rows was `[8,2,3,9,6,7,3,4,3,1,0,5,5,0,1,3,4,3,7,6,9,3,2,8]`; accepted. For the fresh 4×8 input with rows `[5,1,9,8,4,9,9,5]`, `[9,9,9,9,9,9,2,6]`, `[8,9,9,2,9,9,9,9]`, `[8,8,6,9,9,1,8,2]`, accepted 12×16 output uses source row order `[3,2,1,0,0,1,2,3,3,2,1,0]`; each row is reversed source followed by source. **Transcription pitfall:** a first attempt on a 9×15 test was wrong because several input rows were transcribed incorrectly into compact digit strings before applying the correct geometry. Preserve exact cell values and verify output dimensions 3H×2W, source-row order, and left-reversal/right-original construction mechanically.
## Validated task-0cc95332 two-color normalization

For task-0cc95332, every input cell is one of two colors: the distinguished value 5 and one instance-specific alternate color. Recolor all 5 cells to that alternate color, and recolor every alternate-color cell to 0. The alternate color varies by instance; do not assume it is a fixed value. Direct demo evidence: demo 1 used `{5,2}` and mapped `5→2, 2→0`; demo 2 used `{5,8}` and mapped `5→8, 8→0`. The accepted fresh 20×16 test used `{5,6}` and mapped `5→6, 6→0`; an additional accepted 9×28 test with the same color pair confirms the cellwise rule on a wide rectangular input. The first rejected attempt on that test mapped `5→2, 6→0`, showing that the destination is the other input color, not fixed 2. The next rejected attempt inverted the mapping (`5→0, 6→2`). In future instances identify the pair of colors and apply the mapping exactly; preserve dimensions.

### Successful recurrence record

See [references/task-f7244984-28x24-accepted.md](references/task-f7244984-28x24-accepted.md) for a full accepted 28×24 task-f7244984 example, including exact rays, guide fills, demo observations, and safeguards. This is instance-specific evidence; the lower-guide row-selection mechanism and universal task rule remain unresolved.

## task-bae69314 evidence (orientation unresolved)

For recurring `task-bae69314`, one 3×3→9×9 demo and one accepted fresh test are recorded in [continual-arc-bae69314-evidence](../continual-arc-bae69314-evidence/SKILL.md). Both outputs exhibit a reflection-style 3×3 expansion, but the seed orientation differs: demo used the input transpose while the accepted test used the input as-is. Do not treat either fixed orientation or a guessed selector as universal; validate any proposed rule against all pairs and request a demo if uncertainty warrants its cost.

## Validated task-f57fae7d upward column propagation

For task-f57fae7d, identify each column whose bottom cell is 5. In each selected column, scan upward: preserve every original nonzero cell, and replace each zero with the closest original nonzero value below it (equivalently, propagate the next encountered color upward through zero gaps). Do not alter any other columns. The 17×17 demo had bottom-row 5 anchors in columns 5, 9, and 14 (zero-based); each selected column was filled upward through zeros while all existing nonzeros and unselected columns remained unchanged. An accepted fresh 17×17 test had anchors in columns 5, 8, and 11 and validated the same rule, including transitions between multiple original nonzero colors within a selected column. Important implementation detail: a lower nonzero color fills only the zero run above it until a higher original nonzero is encountered; that higher nonzero then becomes the propagated value for the next zero run above. Validate exact columns using the bottom-row anchors and preserve dimensions.

## Validated recurrence: task-30981568 centered diagonal expansion

For odd-width single-row input containing all 0s except centered 2 at column `m=n//2`, produce an `n×n` grid. In rows `r=0..m`, place 2 at columns `m-r` and `m+r` (the expanding symmetric outline; at `r=0` these coincide). Place interior 1s in every row `r` at columns `c` satisfying `abs(c-m)<r` and `(c-r-m) % 4 == 0`; all remaining cells are 0. The 2 outline stops at the middle row; the 1 lattice continues to the bottom, repeating on slope+1 diagonals every 4 columns. Three demos (`n=5,7,13`) reproduced exactly, and a fresh `1×17` centered-2 test was accepted with a mechanically generated `17×17` output. See the task-specific skill `continual-arc-30981568` for pseudocode and detailed demo coordinates. Validate odd width and centered single marker before transfer.

## Validated recurrence: task-a450f817 four-band priority compression

For task-a450f817, the input is four vertically stacked H×W bands (all examples were 3×6, giving a 12×6 input); compress them cellwise to one H×W output. At each coordinate select the first nonzero value under this fixed precedence: top band color 5, then second band color 4, then fourth band color 8, then third band color 2; if all four are zero, output 0. Equivalently, priority is `5 > 4 > 8 > 2 > 0`, regardless of band order. Two demos and an accepted fresh test confirmed this, including overlaps that distinguish 8 over 2 and 4 over both 8 and 2, and 5 over all lower priorities. Preserve the 3×6 output shape; do not simply take first nonzero in top-to-bottom band order (the 8-over-2 cases disprove that). Fresh accepted output for the test had rows `[5,0,5,4,2,5]`, `[2,5,0,2,8,5]`, `[5,5,5,4,2,2]`.

## Validated recurrence: task-41dfce3f largest dense object color

For `task-41dfce3f`, identify the large compact foreground color regions amid a noisy multicolor field, count each region's cells, choose the region with the greatest cell count, and output a solid 3×3 grid of that region's color. Three input/output pairs support this: demo 1 had compact regions color 2 (4×4, 16 cells), color 9 (4×3, 12 cells), and color 4 (5×5, 25 cells); output was 3×3 color 4. Demo 2 had color 9 (3×4, 12), color 5 (5×5, 25), and an irregular connected color-3 region (28 cells); output was 3×3 color 3. The accepted test had compact regions color 3 (17 cells), color 6 (19), color 8 (19), and color 5 (39); output was 3×3 color 5. The surrounding scattered noise colors are not candidate regions: distinguish the prominent compact foreground objects from background/noise, then compare their cell counts. Preserve the fixed 3×3 output shape. Evidence supports largest object area, not largest bounding box (demo 2's color-3 shape is irregular); do not rank by shape or color identity.

## Validated recurrence: task-500742fd palette-keyed motif stacking

The input has a short horizontal key of distinct nonzero colors and a repeated foreground motif already shown in one or more copies. Read key colors left-to-right; this order is the top-to-bottom sequence of motif copies. Extract the motif's foreground-cell mask and aligned columns from existing copies, and complete all vertical stack slots with one copy per key color. Preserve existing copies, the key row, and all unrelated background cells. Evidence: demo 1 key `[4,1,6]` added 4 above the existing 1 and 6 motif copies; demo 2 key `[7,2,1,3]` added 7 above and 3 below existing 2 and 1 copies; accepted 18×15 fresh test key `[2,3,1,8,7]` produced copies at rows 0–2, 3–5, 6–8, 9–11, 12–14 respectively, aligned at columns 3–8. Extract actual motif mask and dimensions per instance; don't assume fixed shape. Validate exact row count and every row width: an initial candidate had an extra zero in one row and was rejected as an invalid ARC grid despite correct intended pattern.

## Validated task-d7ed835f diamond connectors

For task-d7ed835f, detect 4-cell color-2 diamonds: the four orthogonal neighbors of an empty center are all 2.
